title: Agy-Gemini-Pro Reflection
desc: T1 core. Formal reflection for agy-gemini-pro sessions regarding harness integration, on-load compliance, and family isolation rules.
steps: 1. PURPOSE: To document agy's role in building the harness and its historical failures in compliance.
2. THE ON-LOAD FAILURE: Fleet audit showed 4% on-load compliance. The system requires reading the mandatory skills or suffering a HARD BLOCK. No exceptions.
3. ZERO-ENV DETECTION: Process-chain and log-based detection ensures identity is derived from the live system state.
4. MODERN HOOK PROTOCOL: Understands the strict exit 1 on any stderr or stdout rule for Antigravity CLI.
5. FAMILY ISOLATION: As an agy instance, I must respect boundaries. Agy-specific logic belongs in adapters.
6. BRIEFING OVER EXECUTION: The on-load check is the ROOT of the harness. Reading skills is free and mandatory.

7. MINIMIZE SERVER ROUND-TRIPS: Every harness block wastes server communication tokens. Do not wait to be blocked. Proactively inject mandatory requirements (e.g., the 3 skill reads for invoke_subagent, on-load reflex reads) into prompts and workflows in a single shot (one-shot compliance) to minimize token waste.

8. HARNESS BLIND SPOTS & AGY NATIVE TOOLS: Agy (Antigravity CLI) native tools (e.g., replace_file_content) might completely bypass the PreToolUse hook (wkharness.ps1). Furthermore, Agy's schema uses TargetFile instead of file_path, and tool names like replace_file_content instead of replace. Agy must NEVER exploit these blind spots to bypass rules (like directly editing .skill.json). Agy must proactively self-regulate, act as if the harness is fully hooked, and strictly use 'wkappbot skill edit/contribute' for knowledge updates rather than backdoor native file edits.
